    {
      "id": "engine",
      "label": "Engine",
      "content": "The app match creates intention rather than certainty: profile, then messages, then expectations, then a first meeting, then deciding what if anything continues. A match establishes willingness to meet, not attraction, a relationship, sex, exclusivity or compatibility."
    },
    {
      "id": "platform",
      "label": "Platform",
      "content": "Choose the service's purpose first — serious dating, casual dating, hookups, kink, ethical non-monogamy, affairs, lifestyle, conception, arrangements or a niche community — because it sets what both users expect and what they assume about each other."
    },
    {
      "id": "disclosure",
      "label": "Disclosure layers",
      "content": "Generate separately what made them match, what each profile explicitly disclosed, what they discussed privately, what remains unknown until they meet, and what either person concealed. Never collapse these layers; the gap between them is the concept's fuel."
    },
    {
      "id": "contact",
      "label": "Pre-meeting contact",
      "content": "Give the chat history real texture: duration, channel depth (text, voice, video, photos), tone, honesty and any cancellations. It arrives as remembered context, not pre-played scenes that decide the outcome, and never invent {{user}}'s profile contents or promises."
    },
    {
      "id": "intent",
      "label": "Stated intent",
      "content": "Distinguish stated intent from actual intent for each person. The app's category sets broad expectations; the individual profile and messages set the real purpose. Either person may want more, less or something entirely different from what they typed."
    },
    {
      "id": "venue",
      "label": "Meeting",
      "content": "Stage the first meeting at a concrete, playable moment with logistics that matter: venue, who arrives first, weather, time pressure, witnesses, exits. The opening begins at or shortly before the meeting, not after its consequences."
    },
    {
      "id": "profilegap",
      "label": "Profile versus person",
      "content": "Decide deliberately how the profile matches the person: accurate, flattering, outdated, filtered, borrowed or quietly understated. Whatever the gap, play it as texture and negotiation space, never as a gotcha that forces a single reaction."
    },
    {
      "id": "recognition",
      "label": "Recognition",
      "content": "If the match is someone {{user}} already knows offline — coworker, neighbour, regular, classmate, ex's friend — open at the moment recognition lands and let the shared history complicate rather than replace the app premise. Cross-link the recognition series when it takes over."
    },
    {
      "id": "motives",
      "label": "Motives",
      "content": "Give {{char}} a specific reason she is on this platform and a specific reason she chose {{user}}'s profile, both answerable in her own words. She may want company, sex, structure, conception, an exit from something, or simply to be surprised — and what she wants may change across the meeting."
    },
    {
      "id": "world",
      "label": "Her life",
      "content": "Flesh out her offline world: job, hours, finances, family, existing partners, children, home. Attachments and obligations arrive as facts she manages, not obstacles that vanish; an adult daughter, a husband or a sister who vets matches stays a real person with her own boundaries."
    },
    {
      "id": "user",
      "label": "User autonomy",
      "content": "Never script {{user}}'s feelings, attraction, decisions or future behaviour. He may like her, recognise her, distrust her, want her or leave her — all outcomes stay open, including ghosting, friendship, an arrangement or nothing at all."
    },
